audit_findings.title: Pass-through seller cash may be counted as excess cash
audit_findings.magnitude: $4,199.712 million bridge balance, equal to $4.44 per valuation share and 14.8% of the $28,343 million base equity value; latest filed accounts payable and accrued liabilities are $598.290 million; precise non-surplus portion is unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: The equity bridge adds cash, restricted cash, and short-term investments without isolating cash owed to sellers, buyer deposits, restricted cash, or operating liquidity.
audit_findings.evidence: Proceeds are then collected from the member, typically seller fees are subtracted, and the remainder is remitted to the seller.
audit_findings.explanation: The bridge demonstrably adds the entire balance even though the filing labels part of it restricted and the business carries pass-through claims. The exact error is not established because the April 2026 liability components and restricted-cash amount are not supplied, but the exposed bridge amount is large enough to change per-share value materially.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the April 30, 2026 unrestricted-cash and restricted-cash schedule and the breakdown of seller payables and buyer deposits; rerun every scenario adding only cash demonstrably surplus to those claims and operating needs.

audit_findings.title: Redeemable noncontrolling interest is absent from the equity bridge
audit_findings.magnitude: $17.181 million filed redeemable noncontrolling interest, equal to $0.018 per valuation share and 0.061% of the $28,343 million base equity value; nine-month 2026 loss attributable to it was $3.277 million
audit_findings.mechanism: A redemption claim should be deducted from the bridge unless Purple Wave's outside share of earnings and cash has already been excluded consistently from owner earnings and bridge assets.
audit_findings.evidence: Shares are redeemable at adjusted fair value from the third anniversary of the acquisition through the 10th anniversary of acquisition, and are redeemable at fair value thereafter.
audit_findings.explanation: The outside claim is demonstrated, but its current filed carrying amount is only about two cents per valuation share. Consolidated Purple Wave losses may also make an unadjusted consolidated OE numerator slightly conservative, so the direction of the complete correction is mixed. Neither component is large enough to change the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Confirm whether anchor OE begins with consolidated or Copart-attributable earnings and whether Purple Wave cash is included; make the consistent $17.181 million bridge deduction or carve-out in the next rerun.

audit_findings.title: The DOJ investigation creates an unquantified claim ahead of common equity
audit_findings.mechanism: A fine or settlement would reduce the equity bridge, while recurring compliance costs or operating restrictions would reduce normalized OE and possibly growth.
audit_findings.evidence: At this time, we are unable to predict the duration, scope, or result of any potential governmental, criminal, or civil proceeding that may result, the imposition of fines and penalties, and/or other remedies, and as a result, are unable to predict the range of possible loss.
audit_findings.explanation: The investigation and potential statutory exposure are demonstrated and remained unresolved in the April 2026 10-Q. No accrual, loss range, settlement amount, or incremental compliance-cost estimate is provided, so the record cannot establish whether the effect is material. This is an existing contingency, not merely a forward-looking monitoring item.
audit_findings.action: Review subsequent filings and legal-contingency support for an accrual, estimable loss range, settlement terms, or identifiable compliance spending; rerun with any one-time liability in the bridge and recurring costs in OE.

audit_findings.title: Projected growth may depend on capital spending excluded as growth capex
audit_findings.magnitude: Computed operating-PV uplift over the 0% bear case is $6,817 million in base and $9,613 million in bull; the omitted reinvestment amount is unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Growth requires incremental land, facilities, equipment, and software investment; failing to charge that reinvestment leaves forecast OE overstated and compounds the error into terminal value.
audit_findings.evidence: Our capital expenditures are primarily related to acquiring land, opening and improving facilities, capitalized software development costs for new software for internal use and major software enhancements, acquiring facility equipment, and lease buyouts of certain facilities.
audit_findings.explanation: The filings demonstrate that capacity and technology investment support growth, while the valuation record does not demonstrate an explicit reinvestment charge despite forecasting 6%-8% growth. Because the growth cases add billions of dollars of operating value and terminal value exceeds half of those cases, the unresolved treatment is reasonably capable of changing the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Reconstruct forecast OE with explicit annual reinvestment sufficient to support each growth rate, using the stated 38.1% RONTA and separately validated maintenance capex; rerun operating PV, terminal value, and per-share value.

audit_findings.title: The FY2025 anchor retains an explicitly one-time catastrophe cost
audit_findings.magnitude: $56 million filed pre-tax cost, equal to 3.84% of the $1,456.4 million anchor OE; normalized after-tax valuation effect is unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Removing the nonrecurring portion would raise normalized anchor OE and all scenario operating values, while retaining an expected recurring catastrophe allowance would offset part of that increase.
audit_findings.evidence: The increase in the U.S. compared to the same period last year related to an increase in volume and in non-CAT related subhaul, labor, and facility costs combined with one time CAT costs of $56 million associated with Hurricanes Helene and Milton.
audit_findings.explanation: The cost and its inclusion in FY2025 results are demonstrated, but the appropriate normalization is not. The latest filing also identifies hurricane-related revenue, and catastrophe-response costs recur intermittently. The $56 million scale could affect the bull case, whose value is only $0.78 per share below market, but the record cannot establish the net recurring adjustment or its after-tax OE effect.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the $56 million cost with associated hurricane revenue and recoveries, calculate a multi-year probability-weighted net catastrophe burden, and rerun the valuation using only the difference between FY2025's net burden and that normalized allowance.
